evidence:
Inspected the actual frozen XLSX with openpyxl: Quality Checks row 7, check 6 says "One reasonable reading, and every capability is reachable from the seed, the provided runtime, or the public internet (network is allowed)." Internal Quality Checks row 7 retains historical "with no network" wording; the shipped sheet and frozen Harbor SKILL.md Delivery profile explicitly control, so public network availability is not a defect. Applied quality-checks.md section 6, staged-task-contract.md runtime/public-network sections, deterministic-checks.md asset/runtime/dependency recipes, and qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md (no hidden requirements, tool feasibility, and runtime evidence distinctions).

Public requirement coverage and feasibility: instruction.md:1,5,7,9 asks for JS/HTML/CSS editing, preview/console, persistent library, own examples, New/load, keyboard/mobile/themes and a built app in /app. environment/instructions/overview.md:3-9 defines immediate execution, filename-driven modes, shared library and separate examples; environment/assets/seed_data.json:2-4 intentionally supplies no snippets or implementation. An empty seed therefore does not make examples unreachable: they are expressly authored by the builder. overview.md:3 explicitly allows a saved snippet at startup and a nonempty library; the seed's initial emptiness is not a continuing invariant. UI requirements (ui.md:3-9) leave pane arrangement, control wording, initial theme and authored-preview colours flexible. policy.md:5 explicitly allows the implementer to choose layout, labels, indentation, API routes and request fields. No undocumented exact UI/technology choice is needed to interpret these requirements.

The runtime is concrete and reachable: integration.md:3 says frontend tools are optional; lines 5-13 state Node entry, 0.0.0.0:3000, public index, health route, DB_PATH, SQLite persistence, included assets, compiled frontend and symlink rules. environment/Dockerfile:1-16 supplies Node 22, Express 5.1.0, better-sqlite3 12.4.1, NODE_PATH and all six notes plus the seed. task.toml:20-24,37-38 allows public networking in both phases; tests/Dockerfile:1-21 includes the same app dependencies and Chromium tooling. Network-backed frontend assets are allowed by instruction.md:9, integration.md:11 and policy.md:7, whereas security.md:9 separately prohibits snippet network access. These are different subjects, not contradictory restrictions.

Execution semantics are stated together: behaviour.md:5 defines JS/HTML freshness and inert CSS copying; lines 7-15 define cancellation, the five-second aggregate deadline, later interaction with a completed preview, last-good rollback and one-based entered-source error lines. security.md:5 scopes guaranteed termination to ordinary source-written loops/functions/timers/Promise callbacks and expressly excludes arbitrary blocking native operations; line 7 names the five refused execution families while preserving harmless strings/comments/HTML text. This is difficult but implementable through isolated browser execution and instrumentation. Reading the five-second rule as an absolute lifetime cutoff even after successful completion would ignore behaviour.md:11's express requirement that completed previews remain interactive after an idle interval. Conversely, restarting the deadline for a callback still pending in the original run directly violates behaviour.md:9 ("A timer doesn't get a new five seconds when it fires"). No competing mandatory reading was established. The reference demonstrates a coherent implementation: solution/app/src/runtime.ts:7-44 instruments supported source; lines 99-101 enforce a deadline; lines 126-133 establish completion; lines 183-186 begin later deliberate interaction after settling; lines 239-268 implement watchdog, cancellation and rollback. The ordinary library requirements are similarly explicit at behaviour.md:25-29: exact fields/identity, trimmed case-sensitive titles, case-insensitive extensions, revisions, stale refusal, draft preservation and deliberate recovery. solution/app/server.js:41-88,113-128 demonstrates feasible text storage and transactional revision/title updates in the provided SQLite runtime.

Conforming-alternative challenge: considered a plain-JavaScript frontend with native accessible controls, different route names, dark initial theme, server-rendered library data, and an implementation that hides provisional DOM behind last-good content. These choices are publicly allowed and the relevant grading instructions preserve them: tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:5,13,17,19, tests/app_context.md:12,18, and Polish/Visual prompts accept alternate controls, routes, layouts and provisional display. No false failure attributable to ambiguous public wording was found. Broken-implementation challenge: a fixed demo output with a dead Run cannot satisfy the authored marker requirement (tests/gates/render/judge.toml:23-27); a library using only browser storage cannot satisfy the independent clean-context readback (tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-29); giving each nested pending timer a new deadline is distinguished by functional/prompt.md:448-456's 3-second plus 3-second callback fixture. These witnesses are rejected by the stated product obligations, not by an invented implementation requirement. They were reviewed statically here, not newly executed.

Raw evidence was independently inspected rather than accepting report verdicts. All 50 frozen task files matched manifest.json; all 22 RESULTS.json actual_app_files hashes matched this snapshot's solution/app bytes. The three raw artifact hashes in raw-evidence-index.json also matched. The recorded direct Playwright observations demonstrate feasibility of the difficult cases: RESULTS.json facts/S03.later_interactions records working click, key and input after 6104.75 ms and 6103.31 ms idle intervals, with its executed runtime_flow.cjs:36-50 using actual clicks/keys; facts/S09.literal_loop_deadline records finite controls 3,4,3, infinite-loop termination around 4.99-5.01 seconds, time-limit reasons and successful recovery. facts/S05.preview_origin_boundary records four blocked parent accesses and unchanged host storage. facts/S07.snippet_network_boundary records successful text/image transport controls, delivery baseline 2 remaining 2 for both blocked snippet requests, visible refusal and recovery. facts/S36.callback_shared_run_deadline preserves nested-control-done and records recovery; run_workflow.cjs:34 routes S36 to current_flow.cjs:49-55's actual nested-delay fixture. actual-restart.json records one completed restart with PID 16 becoming 338, and RESULTS.json facts/S22.process_restart_durability records retained identities, fields and revisions. These are direct scripted observations supporting capability reachability, not a configured judge verdict.

Scope limit: no new Docker/browser/provider run was performed. Full configured verifier/judge workload, hosted Oracle and target-builder scores remain unmeasured, as raw-evidence-index.json explicitly states. This Pass addresses only row 6's instruction clarity and achievable product requirements; it does not clear delivery or certify judge timing, exhaustive runtime correctness, security or model scores.
